text:
maya: Heads up — after last night's Cilium rollout (1.15.1) we're seeing intermittent east-west packet loss between GPU pods in us-west2. Affected pods are in the same node-pool; traffic to other node-pools looks flakier.

alvaro: seeing the same. latency spikes + retransmits on tcp flows. GPU training jobs hit checkpoints failing due to RPC timeouts.

maya: quick iperf3 from pod-a -> pod-b (same AZ):
```
iperf3 -c 10.2.34.12 -t 30
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  4]   0.00-30.00  sec  1.42 GBytes   406 Mbits/sec  (retransmits ~7%)
```

cheng: from node level I see occasional Rx errors on veth interfaces and kernel dmesg with: 
```
[  +0.123456] cilium_vxlan: vxlan_recv: bad checksum
[  +0.000321] ip6_frag: fragment missing
```

kevin: cilium-agent logs show a lot of L7 & ENCAP warnings right after the daemonset update: `Warning: encap mtu mismatch, dropping pkt` and `redirect: unable to program becuase of route conflict` (typo preserved in logs).

infra-oncall: rolling back to 1.14.3 is an option but it's a big change. Can we confirm if host MTU changed or if kube-proxy iptables rules were rewritten during the upgrade?

maya: I checked host MTU — still 9000 on NIC. Pod MTU reported 1450 inside pod, which is expected for vxlan. But I found inconsistent MTU values on some nodes: two nodes show 1400 inside the host-bridge.

alvaro: that explains some of the fragmentation causing retransmits. Could the cilium upgrade have toggled offload settings (GRO/TSO) or changed default encapsulation (vxlan vs geneve)?

cheng: we patched configmap -> `tunnel: vxlan` unchanged. But Cilium now auto-detects ENCAP mode when SR-IOV is present; a bug in detection path could flip modes on a subset of nodes.

maya: repro steps I ran: scale 20 GPU pods across 3 nodes, run all-pairs iperf matrix, then kill cilium-agent on one node and watch failures cascade.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2301. Paging infra-oncall.

infra-oncall: thanks. Next steps: 1) collect cilium-agent logs from nodes with errors 2) dump CNI state (`cilium status`, `cilium bpf tunnel list`) 3) capture `ip link` and `ip route` from host and pod 4) run non-encap test (hostNetwork pods) to confirm overlay vs host issue.

kevin: grabbing logs now. snippet from cilium-agent on node-3: 
```
level=warning msg="node mismatched encap mtu" node=node-3 encap_mtu=1400 expected=1450
level=error msg="programming redirect failed: file exists" err="EEXIST"
```

maya: non-encap hostNetwork ping tests are green between same hosts, so overlay seems the problem.

alvaro: curious — are we hitting RDMA NICs with SR-IOV on these GPU nodes? I recall one provider image enabled SR-IOV VF drivers last month. RDMA + encapsulation sometimes interacts badly with GRO/TSO.

cheng: yes some GPU nodes have SR-IOV VFs for passthrough. I see `ib0` on NICs on two nodes. Cilium's detection handler has a codepath that skips encapsulation for RDMA devices, maybe a race where some nodes were flagged differently during the rolling upgrade.

maya: proposal: pin Cilium to `1.15.1-rc2 -> rollback to 1.14.3` for the next 2 hours to stabilize jobs; in parallel run a canary of 1.15.1 with env var `ENABLE_RDMA_DETECT=false` on a small subset.

infra-oncall: agree on canary. But rollback plan: need to ensure BGP/NodeRoutes are consistent. Rolling DS rollback will restart cilium agents sequentially; we must cordon one node at a time and drain GPU pods carefully.

kevin: created a canary daemonset patch: `--set runcFlags=... ENABLE_RDMA_DETECT=false` applied to 3 nodes via nodeSelector. Initial results: canary pods show stable iperf ~9xx Mbps, retransmits 0-1%.

maya: meanwhile we noticed policy enforcement rules were rehashed and a handful of NetworkPolicies got more specific due to a config generator script running during the upgrade window — could be unrelated but complicates debugging.

alvaro: posted a gist with full `ip link`, `cilium bpf tunnel list`, and iperf matrix: https://gist.github.com/redwood/net-debug-1752901234 (internal).

cheng: action items I will take: 1) correlate nodes with SR-IOV/RDMA to those reporting encap_mtu mismatch 2) open a quick issue with Cilium upstream (include logs + minimal repro) 3) run a test with GRO/TSO disabled on host to see effect.

infra-oncall: I'll initiate the rollback to 1.14.3 on the non-canary nodepool (cordon+drain pattern) — will post progress here.

ops-bot: rollback job started for nodes [node-1,node-4,node-5].

maya: update: after rolling back cilium on node-1, training jobs resumed on that node, iperf looks clean. Still seeing 1-2 problematic nodes.

kevin: suggestion: add a pre-upgrade check in our upgrade playbook to detect SR-IOV/RDMA and force a specific encap mode or skip upgrade.

maya: Agreed. Also add a quick verification step to run an iperf matrix and check `encap_mtu` across nodes post-upgrade.

alvaro: once canary is stable for 30m and rollback finishes, we should schedule a maintenance window with Cilium maintainers to walk through the detection logic.

cheng: filed GH issue: cilium/cilium#98765 — includes logs, repro script, and tags: mtu, rdma, encap, upgrade.

maya: thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated and follow up with postmortem + action items for the upgrade playbook. :white_check_mark:
